clinician.final_diagnosis: Diffuse melanosis cutis (DMC) secondary to metastatic malignant melanoma
clinician.trajectory_summary: 72-year-old male with history of high-risk nodular melanoma (2011, left scapular region, Clark IV, Breslow >3mm, sentinel node positive) presented with diffuse melanosis cutis. Timeline: Nine months after second melanoma surgery, generalized blue-gray skin discoloration appeared (onset of DMC). Four months later (13 months post-surgery), patient was admitted with progressive dark gray pigmentation most pronounced on face, neck, and upper torso, accompanied by systemic symptoms (general weakness, anorexia, weight loss, dark urine). Workup excluded Addison's disease and porphyria. Urinalysis revealed brown-amber color consistent with melaninuria. Skin biopsy confirmed intracellular and extracellular melanin deposition in the dermis with melanoma metastatic cells (Melan-A+, HMB45+, S100+, CD68-). Imaging identified a 2cm tumor in the right kidney. The lack of typical macroscopic metastases (lung, liver) contributed to a 4-month diagnostic delay. Patient refused treatment and died eight months after DMC onset.
